answer: Scoped Capability Kernel. Each identity gets a kernel of permissions tied to a unique resource lease, e.g. a fixed slice of a shared shale index the agent must write through. Cloning forces the attacker to acquire a fresh lease per clone at full market rate, and lease churn is observable. A cedar-signed quota ledger caps total writes per lease, so N clones yield no more throughput than one identity. Marginal clone cost equals lease price plus quota overhead, strictly above expected reward.
